statement: Split routing compares keys with a typed comparator: resolveSplitTargetPartitionId's raw `value < metadata.splitKey` JavaScript relational comparison is replaced by a type-aware comparator (numeric vs string vs buffer) owned in one module, mixed-type key spaces are rejected with a typed outcome instead of silently mis-routing, and the same comparator is used by every split routing decision (mirror replay, snapshot batching, query routing). doneWhen: the test-receipt probe reads solve/evidence/split-key-comparator-typing.receipt.json with outstanding 0 — typed-comparator-owned, mixed-type-rejection, and single-comparator-call-sites receipts all passing.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.
Each new regression test must fail when the corresponding mechanism is reverted while the rest of the change remains.
The oracle evidence files must be written by a deterministic evidence harness that re-runs the recorded proof commands (focused test files, red-on-revert probes) and writes the receipt artifact.

A key whose type is incomparable to the splitKey type must never be routed by JavaScript's arbitrary relational coercion (F12): reject with a typed outcome rather than routing a row to the wrong child.
